Rashi on Menachot 2a:1:1.hebrew: כל המנחות שנקמצו שלא לשמן - כגון שהתנדב מנחת מרחשת והביאה, וקמצה הכהן ואמר: הריני קומץ לשם מחבת:
Rashi on Menachot 2a:1:1.english: All the meal offerings from which a handful was removed not for their sake - For example, where one volunteered a deep-pan meal offering and brought it, and the priest removed a handful from it and said: "I am hereby removing a handful for the sake of a shallow-pan [meal offering]."

Rashi on Menachot 2a:1:2.english: Fit - And their handful is burned [on the altar], and their remainder is eaten [by the priests].

Rashi on Menachot 2a:1:3.hebrew: אלא שלא עלו לבעלים לשם חובה - דלא יצא ידי נדרו, וצריך להביא אחרת לשם מרחשת:
Rashi on Menachot 2a:1:3.english: Except that they did not count for the owner toward [his] obligation - For he did not fulfill his vow, and he must bring another [meal-offering] for the sake of a *marcheshet* [deep pan].

Rashi on Menachot 2a:1:4.hebrew: חוץ ממנחת חוטא - כגון ההיא דמטמא מקדש, דכתיב בויקרא: ואם לא תשיג ידו לשתי תורים וגו':
Rashi on Menachot 2a:1:4.english: Except for the meal offering of a sinner - For example, that [meal offering] of one who defiles the Temple, as it is written in Leviticus: "And if his means do not suffice for two turtledoves, etc."

Rashi on Menachot 2a:1:5.hebrew: ומנחת קנאות - מנחת סוטה, שאם קמצן שלא לשמן, כגון לשם נדבה, או נתן בכלי את הקומץ שלא לשמן, או הוליך או הקטיר שלא לשמן, או חישב באחת מעבודות הללו: הריני עובד לשמו ושלא לשמו:
Rashi on Menachot 2a:1:5.english: And the meal offering of jealousy - The meal offering of a sota [a woman suspected of infidelity], for if [the priest] removed a handful from them not for their sake, such as for the sake of a voluntary offering, or placed the handful into a vessel not for their sake, or conveyed or burned [it] not for their sake, or had intention during one of these services: "I am performing [the service] for its sake and not for its sake" [they are disqualified].

Rashi on Menachot 2a:2:1.hebrew: או שלא לשמו ולשמו - באלו שתי מנחות פסולין, ואין שיריהן נאכלין, וטעמא מפ' בגמ'. והא דתנא או שלא לשמו ולשמו, דלא תימא: לשמו ושלא לשמו הוא דפסולה, דתפיס לשון אחרון, אבל שלא לשמו ולשמו לא — קמ"ל דאף בתחלת דבריו אדם נתפס אית לן:
Rashi on Menachot 2a:2:1.english: Or not for its sake and for its sake - In [the case of] these two meal offerings, they are disqualified and their remainders are not eaten, and the reason is explained in the Gemara. And as for that which [the tanna] taught, "or not for its sake and for its sake" — so that you should not say that it is [only in the case of] "for its sake and not for its sake" that it is disqualified, for one holds to the final expression, but [in the case of] "not for its sake and for its sake" it is not [disqualified]; [therefore,] it teaches us that we hold [that] a person is held even to the beginning of his statement.

Rashi on Menachot 2a:5:1.hebrew: מדקתני אלא, משמע דכל דינה כמנחה כשירה, אלא זה בלבד:
Rashi on Menachot 2a:5:1.english: From the fact that [the mishna] taught "except" [ella], it implies that all its laws are like [those of] a valid meal offering, except for this alone.

Rashi on Menachot 2a:5:2.hebrew: ואסור לשנויי - בה שינוי אחר, כגון אם עבר וקמצה שלא לשמה, אסור לתת קומץ בכלי שלא לשמה:
Rashi on Menachot 2a:5:2.english: And it is prohibited to deviate - [By making] another deviation in it; for example, if one transgressed and removed a handful from it not for its own sake, it is prohibited to place the handful into a vessel not for its own sake.

Rashi on Menachot 2a:7:1.hebrew: נדבה - בתמיה: והא נדר הוא, דכתיב כאשר נדרת (דברים כג):
Rashi on Menachot 2a:7:1.english: A gift offering - [This is said] in astonishment: But is it not a vow, as it is written: "As you have vowed" (Deuteronomy 23)?

Rashi on Menachot 2a:7:2.hebrew: אם כמה שנדרת עשית - לשמה, יהא נדר, כלומר: יצאת ידי נדרך. ואם לאו, יהא נדבה, ויביא אחרת לנדרו:
Rashi on Menachot 2a:7:2.english: If you acted in accordance with what you vowed - [If you offered it] for its own sake, it shall be a vow offering, meaning: you have fulfilled your vow. And if not, it shall be a gift offering, and he must bring another [offering] for his vow.

Tosafot on Menachot 2a:1:2.hebrew: שלא לשמן - לכאורה משמע דאיירי בשינוי קודש, כדמפרש בסיפא: לשם מנחת חוטא, לשם מנחת נדבה. והוא הדין שנוי בעלים, כדמוכח בגמרא בפ"ק דזבחים (דף ד.). ושמא פשיטא ליה להש"ס בכל דוכתי דשנוי בעלים כשנוי קדש, כתירוצו של רבה דמשני בגמרא: כאן בשנוי קדש, כאן בשנוי בעלים; אי נמי, ממתני' דפרק בית שמאי (זבחים דף מו:): לשם ששה דברים הזבח נזבח, לשם זבח, לשם זובח:
Tosafot on Menachot 2a:1:2.english: Not for their sake - At first glance, it implies that [the mishna] is dealing with a change of sanctity [shinui kodesh], as it explains in the latter clause: "For the sake of a sinner's meal offering, for the sake of a voluntary meal offering." And the same applies to a change of owner [shinui ba'alim], as is proven in the Gemara in the first chapter of Zevachim (4a). And perhaps it is obvious to the Talmud in all places that a change of owner is like a change of sanctity, like the resolution of Rabba, who answers in the Gemara: "Here [it refers to] a change of sanctity; here [it refers to] a change of owner"; or alternatively, from the mishna in chapter Beit Shammai (Zevachim 46b): "For the sake of six things the sacrifice is slaughtered: For the sake of the sacrifice, for the sake of the sacrificer."

Tosafot on Menachot 2a:2:1.english: For their sake and not for their sake - In the first chapter of Zevachim (folio 2b), we conclude that [the Tanna] means that their unspecified [intent] is considered as [being] for their sake.

Tosafot on Menachot 2a:7:1.hebrew: קרי ליה נדר וקרי ליה נדבה - משמע מהכא, דכל היכא דכתיב נדר — נדר דוקא, ונדבה — נדבה דווקא; וכן בפ"ק דר"ה (דף ו.) לענין בל תאחר. ואפילו לר"מ דפ"ק דחולין (דף ב. ושם: ד"ה אבל) דדריש: טוב אשר לא תדור — טוב מזה ומזה שאינו נודב כל עיקר, אלמא קרי לנדבה נדר — שאני הכא, דדריש מדשני קרא בדיבוריה. אי נמי, בחולין דריש, דכיון דחייש קרא לתקלה, לא שנא נדר ולא שנא נדבה, דבתרוייהו איכא למיחש. אי נמי, משום דנדר נפקא לן מכי תחדל, שמע מינה דטוב אשר לא תדור לנדבה אתא:
Tosafot on Menachot 2a:7:1.english: It calls it a vow and it calls it a gift offering - It implies from here that wherever "vow" [neder] is written, [it means] specifically a vow, and [wherever] "gift offering" [nedava] [is written, it means] specifically a gift offering; and so [it implies] in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (folio 6a) regarding [the prohibition of] "you shall not delay" [bal te'aḥer]. And even according to Rabbi Meir in the first chapter of Chullin (folio 2b, and there, s.v. Aval), who expounds: "'Better that you do not vow' (Ecclesiastes 5:4) — better than both of these is one who does not volunteer [an offering] at all," which shows that [the verse] calls a gift offering a "vow" — here it is different, for [the Gemara] expounds [its question] from [the fact] that the verse changed its wording. Alternatively, in Chullin it expounds [the verse thus] because since Scripture is concerned for a mishap, there is no difference between a vow and a gift offering, as in both of them there is reason for concern. Alternatively, because [refraining from] a vow is derived for us from "When you refrain [from vowing]" (Deuteronomy 23:23), conclude from it that "Better that you do not vow" came [to refer] to a gift offering.

Tosafot on Menachot 2a:7:2.hebrew: ואם לאו יהא נדבה - אע"ג דבפ"ק דראש השנה (דף ו.) דריש ליה לענין בל תאחר, דלא שייך לאחר שחיטה, הכא דריש מפשטיה דקרא, דמשמע דקרי ליה לנדר נדבה:
Tosafot on Menachot 2a:7:2.english: And if not, let it be a voluntary offering - Even though in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (6a) it expounds it regarding the matter of bal te'aḥer [the prohibition against delaying], which does not apply after slaughter, here [the Gemara] expounds [it] from the plain meaning of the verse, which implies that it calls a vow a voluntary offering.
